title: Who Will Arise and Plead My Right
description: Who Will Arise and Plead My Right in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 94, part 2, headed “God our support and comfort; or, Deliverance from temptation and persecution”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Who will a-rise and plead my right A-gainst my nu-merous foes, While earth and hell their force u-nite, And all my hopes op-pose?

lines: Who will arise and plead my right
While earth and hell their force unite,
Had not the Lord, my rock, my help,
My life had now in silence dwelt,
Thy grace stood constant by my side,
Thy boundless love forgives my faults,
But God, my refuge, rules the skies,
Let malice vent her rage aloud,
The Lord our God shall judge the proud,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
